about.we_sell: Invented example. Route-planning software for companies that run their own delivery fleets.
about.buyer: Invented example. Heads of operations, logistics and fleet at distributors; the COO signs, the dispatch or fleet manager champions it.
sources: invented for this example; a real rubric lists where each part came from

rules.label: Account fit
rules.miss_says: at a low-fit or unscored account

bands.says: started this role in the last 4 months
in this role under a year
in this role over a year

questions.label: Buying role
questions.instructions: For software that plans delivery routes, which role would the person with job title `title` most likely play in the purchase?

decision_maker.means: Owns operations or logistics budget: COO, VP or Head of Operations, Logistics or Supply Chain.

champion.means: Runs the fleet or dispatch day to day: fleet, dispatch, transportation or distribution manager.

influencer.means: Consulted but does not own it: IT, finance, procurement.

not_involved.means: Unrelated to operations or logistics: sales, marketing, HR, engineering and similar.

questions.label: Seniority
questions.instructions: How senior is the job title `title`?
levels: Director or head of a function

questions.label: Not a prospect
questions.instructions: Is this person a recruiter, a student, a job seeker, or an outside consultant rather than an employee in an operating role?

criteria.true: Recruiter, student, intern, job seeker, or external consultant or advisor.
criteria.false: An employee in an operating role at the company.

questions.says_yes: not a prospect (recruiter, student or outsider)
